verdicts.evidence: The 'no runward/adr/' guard is skipped: adrFilename goes from null to an ENOENT throw (measured at function level on a missionDir without adr/). Surface: collectSealableEvidence, hence the attestation digest and the freeze. Measured recipe: copy of examples/request-triage, rm -r runward/adr (the applied adr:0001 row remains); `check --attest` shipped: exit 1 AND the full in-toto Statement on stdout (the attestation of a red verdict is an artifact the pipeline consumes); mutated: exit 1 with '✗ ENOENT: no such file or directory, scandir .../runward/adr' and NO Statement — the verdict artifact is replaced by an infrastructure error that sends the operator down a false trail. The --freeze path is only protected by accident: checked that a mission without adr/ is never green (even the n/a-row variant stays red, 'refusing to seal'), so collect does not run there. Why nothing sees it: every fixture in the legs goes through init, which always scaffolds adr/; smoke, audit-corpus, intoto-schema and self-gate replayed on the mutated build: all green.

verdicts.evidence: NO mutant of this function moves the probe, so a DEDICATED CONTROL was built rather than concluding from an absence: replacing `out.set(line[1].toLowerCase(), id)` with an arbitrary key, and inverting `if (!line)`, each make the probe diverge (`natures|*` lines). So the probe is sensitive to it. What these mutants touch is redundant or unreachable work across the 16 journal layouts measured: sorting a list of files that is then walked in full, a `/^ADR-.*\.md$/i` filter whose removal only adds files that no other rule accepts, two `catch { continue }` that only a concurrent I/O error would reach, and the anchors of a regex whose `**Nature not carried**:` label is at the start of the line in every ADR form this product reads. The declaration remains a DISCLOSURE (ADR-0075): it crosses no gate, so none of these mutants can move a verdict. METHOD OF THIS PASS (identical for every verdict below, closed on 2026-09-18). The mutant is APPLIED to the build, a behaviour probe calls the product on inputs that reach the mutated line, and a canonical digest of 250+ observations is compared: pointer grammar over 34 cells, manifest sections over 12 documents (renamed heading, lowercase, deep, last, duplicated, inside a code block, unclosed block), decision journals over 16 layouts, nine real missions read by evidenceReport/evidenceBreakdown/collectSealableEvidence/requiresLedger/prosePointerLedger/computeVerdict in strict AND non-strict, and the exact bounds of the signature guard (30, 119, 120, 121, 511, 512, 513). COVERAGE VERIFIED: the 56 instructed survivors are all on a line the probe EXECUTES, measured by NODE_V8_COVERAGE taking the innermost range (the first version marked 1540 lines out of 1540 and measured nothing). SENSITIVITY PROVEN: on this same pass, 20 mutants moved the probe and are now KILLED by tests written after reading the difference — so the instrument does tell what changes from what does not. The probe was wrong six times before it was right, and its failure mode was always to answer "equivalent": branches not reached, messages cut at 200 characters, verdict truncated at 4000, wrong mutated occurrence chosen. Each correction surfaced changing mutants that would have been filed wrongly.
